speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Grassroots Organisations (GROs) have always played an important role in enabling the Government's efforts to support residents by raising awareness of and, in some cases, directly administering national schemes, such as the Community Development Council (CDC) Vouchers Scheme, on the ground.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Many GROs would be activated to support the administration of these schemes, which typically involves processing at least 260,000 such applications each year.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Over the years, GROs have also initiated their own local welfare assistance schemes to provide assistance to their residents having regard to the specific needs of their local demographic, which these GROs assess.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These local schemes complement the national schemes, often helping those who fall through the cracks.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The assistance and support from the Government, GROs and community partners have had a real impact on the livelihood of our population.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For instance, the cash distributions initiated by GROs and community partners help low-income households alleviate the increased expenses during festive seasons as they prepare for celebrations with their families.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Heartland hawkers and merchants were able to obtain relief from the pandemic and rising costs of living with the CDC Vouchers Scheme.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They could not have done so without the prompt reimbursement of the voucher claims facilitated by the GROs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They do so by raising awareness and identifying eligible households and assessing applications, including from those who might marginally miss the criteria of these schemes or require some form of additional assistance.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: People's Association (PA) staff and volunteers are then mobilised to extend the last-mile support under these schemes by directly administering the distribution of welfare assistance or vouchers from the Government or community partners.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In doing so, PA staff and volunteers have developed a good understanding of the ground needs and often had to be flexible as well to render timely assistance to the residents.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about the proportion of GROs that were audited by the AGO.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I said, there are about 2,000 GROs across Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Each year, the AGO decides on which organisation it wishes to audit – this includes the GROs – and how many it wishes to audit.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The AGO also retains discretion to determine the areas to be covered in its audit and the approach to take.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I will explain to Members now the facts of these two cases.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The first case concerned the management of monies for welfare distribution at festive events by one GRO.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Welfare distributions to low-income residents at festive events are a form of local welfare assistance scheme initiated by the GROs, often in collaboration with community partners.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This, as I said, complements the national schemes in rendering support to the vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Such schemes are not uncommon and most GROs would have their local schemes to address the specific local needs of each constituency.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In auditing the disbursement procedure of this scheme, the AGO found that a crossed cheque was issued to a staff member.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When the cheque was brought to the bank by the staff member, it would be processed and the amount would be deposited into the staff member's bank account.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The staff member would then withdraw the deposited amount in cash over the bank counter, accompanied by one other staff member.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Verification of the cash withdrawn would be performed by a third staff member not involved in the cash withdrawal.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Throughout this process, the deposit and withdrawal would be tagged to the individual responsible in PA's Financial Accounting System that is used by all GROs to account for receipts and payments.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The monies withdrawn were then distributed to the scheme recipients, with proper record and accounting of the amounts given out.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked what the standard procedure would otherwise have been.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When the uncrossed cheque is brought to the bank, the cash would be withdrawn immediately over the counter and retained by the staff concerned and then applied to the scheme for disbursement.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There are a few notable points from this case.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: First, whilst this was not the correct procedure, the staff concerned explained that it was thought that the additional step in using the crossed cheque was taken to better account for the money.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And that was why that step was taken.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Second, the monies withdrawn were duly checked and verified through the process by multiple and different staff members.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Third, all the amounts deposited, withdrawn and distributed were properly recorded and accounted for.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The AGO has reviewed the records and found no evidence of loss or misappropriation of monies in this case.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The practice ceased once the AGO noted this observation in the course of its audit.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The second case concerned the reimbursement of monies to the hawkers and merchants under the CDC Voucher scheme at one GRO.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The CDC Voucher scheme was launched by the PA in 2020 to help lower-income households defray their cost of living and, at the same time, support hawkers and heartland merchants who were affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: At that time, GROs helped to administer the scheme by distributing the physical vouchers to the low-income households, as well as thereafter, facilitating the reimbursement of voucher claims from the hawkers and merchants.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The period in question coincided with the time when cashflow of hawkers and merchants were seriously affected by the COVID-19 pandemic and various other measures, including safe management measures.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The GRO in question thus saw a need to set up a system which could facilitate a prompt claims process for the hawkers and merchants under the scheme.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For this case, the AGO found that the process took place as follows: staff collected the used physical vouchers from the hawkers and merchants, and tabulated the amount to be reimbursed to each of them on a weekly basis.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The transaction volume was high, with most of the claims of small amounts at around $20 to $30.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Members would recall that this first iteration of the CDC Voucher schemes was entirely physical; physical vouchers were used.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To facilitate these reimbursements, a crossed cheque would be issued by the GRO to the relevant staff member's name, who would withdraw cash and then reimburse the hawkers and merchants using this cash withdrawn.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When the hawkers and merchants received the monies from the staff, they would indicate their receipt of the cash by signing against the listings prepared by the staff member.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Similar to the first case, the process deviated from the standard procedure in that a crossed cheque was issued instead of an uncrossed cheque and the monies went through the staff member's personal bank account briefly.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: However, there were proper records and accounting of all the claims and the disbursement of monies.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This arrangement ceased with the changes to the CDC Voucher scheme in December 2021 when electronic vouchers were introduced in place of physical ones.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Thus far, we have identified three other cases in which similar inappropriate practice of money management for welfare assistance schemes was adopted.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In all of these cases, there was also no loss of funds nor any mala fides in staff conduct.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: PA has also implemented and will continue to work on strengthening its internal governance and oversight of key processes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I would add that given the scale and volume of such transactions, which I have outlined to Members earlier, PA recognises that staff and volunteers do face challenges when administering welfare assistance schemes and other Government programmes and, at the same time, managing administrative matters, such as contracts and claims processes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: PA will continue to identify ways to improve its structures, systems as well as processes to mitigate such reoccurrence, but at the same time allow the GROs and its volunteers to do what it does best on the ground by delivering last-mile services direct to residents, helping them in times of need and making sure – as Members saw in the case of the welfare schemes during COVID-19 – that cash flow, which was vital during COVID-19, was not affected.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Sharael Taha, Ms He Ting Ru, Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Leong Mun Wai asked about PA's plans to strengthen compliance and prevent future occurrence.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In recent years, PA has embarked on major structural changes and implemented measures to strengthen its key governance processes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These were to address risks that were observed through past AGO audit findings as well as picked up through PA's regular internal audits and reviews.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It has put in place a systematic plan that includes accelerating the full implementation of measures we had embarked on in recent years.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Digitalising manual processes to minimise the need for cash handling, refining financial procurement rules and bolstering capabilities of staff and GROs and their volunteers in these areas.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: PA will also address the lapses identified and strengthen the monitoring and compliance to procedures and processes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The review committee will regularly report the progress of the implementation to the PA board as well as to MCCY.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: PA will update the public on its progress from time to time.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: PA takes the findings of the AGO very seriously and will continue on taking the steps outlined above to address the gaps in the processes.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: If we look at the second part of my original Parliamentary Question, it is really in terms of whether there was any form of disciplinary actions that are taken on the staff who were involved in the transfer and even the management team, and whether there was any censure of the board as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The relevant authorisations were all disclosed and properly recorded in the systems maintained by the GRO and that, as I mentioned earlier, was precisely the reason why AGO was able to check and verify, based on these records, that no money was missing at all.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In relation to the Member's question about follow-up steps for the staff and the volunteers, I have set them out in my response.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We have underscored the importance of adhering to this and counselled the relevant parties concerned to ensure that this does not occur again.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We are approaching the end of Question Time.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will allow for a few more clarifications.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, keep it short and keep the answer short as well.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Second question: are there simpler ways to allow the use of PA or grassroots bank accounts for fund disbursement purposes and disallow the use of PA staff personal bank accounts for such purposes?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As we move towards ensuring that we undertake transactions digitally, there will be a constituency of persons, usually the elderly, who are not able to keep up and process the transactions in the same way.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, what we do at PA is we always go with the mantra that we say it is digital first, but not digital only.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, those of our seniors or other residents who come and need assistance because they are unable to process or handle the transactions digitally, we will assist them in person and, in some cases, if necessary, we will help them to print the hard copies so that they will be able to administer.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But, at the same time, in our drive to ensure that we move towards digital transactions, our staff is also trained to counsel such people to help them and try and get them on board the digital framework so that, for future transactions, they will be more equipped and more assured to be able to handle those transactions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To the Member's second question, the proper process, as Members have heard me outline, is indeed to avoid co-mingling with the staff's bank account.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In this case, what happened was that the cheque was crossed and, as a result, had to be deposited in the staff's account.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The usual process is for the cheques to be uncrossed and for cash to be handled across the counter without entering the staff's bank account.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: First, I understand from the Minister's reply that there is undertaking to be done to make certain checks that are similar in scope.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Can the Minister share about the timeline for when this is expected to be completed and also a bit more details about the scope in which these additional checks are going to be carried out?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Can I also ask about the composition of this committee?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Are they external to the PA or are they appointed from external sources?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The scope of its work is essentially to look at its current processes, give a view and to really have a second pair of eyes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In most of these cases, it is not that the process is not set out.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The process has been set out, there are standard operating procedures (SOPs), and in fact, that is why the AGO was able to audit it and make these findings of inconsistency relative to what the SOP ought to be.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But I will convey the point and discuss it with the review committee.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Member's first question is on the scope of the checks.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Obviously, as we do this, even as we focus on those transactions, the lessons learnt can be adopted on a broader scale, such as co-mingling is not just prohibited in the context of welfare assistance schemes, but also across the board.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, those are lessons that we will pick up from this review but applied across a broader variety of different transactions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix, unless Members had asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn.]
